name: CPM-HA20G

lead: CPM-HA20G is a cohesive polydensified matrix hyaluronic acid with glycerol, marketed by Merz as Belotero Revive. Rather than adding volume, it is microinjected into the skin to improve its quality: hydration, firmness, smoothness and glow.
Small randomised and open-label studies report improvements in elasticity, hydration, pore volume and tone after a series of sessions spaced weeks apart.

paras: A clinician places it in the dermis or immediate subdermal layer of areas such as the cheeks in a course of sessions about four weeks apart in the published studies. Techniques studied include serial puncture, blunt cannula and multi-needle devices.

Common effects of HA injections include bruising, redness, pain and itching; rarer ones include infection, allergic reactions and lumps. Vascular occlusion with vision loss is a rare, serious filler risk described in the wider literature.

chain: Microinjected HA with glycerol in the dermis
angle.text: CPM-HA20G targets skin texture and radiance instead of volume. Studies measured gains in firmness, hydration and pore appearance on the cheeks.

lead: CPM-HA20G is a low-viscoelasticity hyaluronic acid (HA) filler with glycerol, sold as Belotero Revive by Merz Pharmaceuticals; the HA is slightly cross-linked at 20 mg/ml with 17.5 mg/ml glycerol [1]. It is used as a skin booster, injected superficially to improve skin quality rather than to reshape the face [2][3].
People seek it for a fresher, firmer, smoother and more even-looking complexion. Studies have measured skin glow, firmness, pore size, tone evenness and hydration [3][4].
Published work consists mostly of small randomised, split-face and open-label studies, several of them sponsored or run around the manufacturer's product [2][3][4][1][5][6].
infobox: Cohesive polydensified matrix HA with glycerol [1]

paras: The product is used for early signs of facial skin ageing and general skin-quality improvement [6]. Studies have also looked at enlarged pores [4].

In a randomised trial of fifteen subjects, one or three treatments with CPM-HA20G into the lower cheeks improved skin firmness, and the multiple-treatment group also improved on skin fatigue and density with stable thickness [2].
A 24-week open-label study of twenty Korean women found improvements in skin glow, firmness, surface evenness, tone evenness and transepidermal water loss at weeks 12 and 24 [3].
A post-market study of 25 women reported increased elasticity, firmness, tone, radiance and hydration, with some effects lasting up to 36 weeks [6].

Fillers based on HA commonly cause bruising, redness, pain and itching; less commonly infection and allergic reactions, and rarely vascular occlusion leading to vision loss or skin necrosis [7]. In the US the FDA regulates dermal fillers as medical devices [7].

A randomised three-versus-one session study (n=15) reported significant firmness gains [2]. A 2025 open-label study in Korean women (n=20) reported gains across glow, firmness, evenness and tone [3]. A 2025 split-face randomised study of 30 subjects compared CPM-HA20 with CPM-HA20G for enlarged pores; both reduced pore volume, with a 24.2% greater reduction on the glycerol-containing side [4]. A split-face study compared CPM-HA20G with a hybrid cooperative complex HA (Profhilo) in 24 women, with both showing effects on hydration, elasticity, water loss and melanin [1]. A 2026 case series compared serial puncture, blunt cannula and multi-needle delivery with ultrasound confirmation, finding comparable improvements [5].

timeline.event: Post-market study of CPM-HA20G (Belotero Revive) for early skin ageing is published [6].
